The Discourse on the Absence of Untimely Death for an Arahant: Is there no untimely death for an Arahant?
Yes, there is.
Is there no killer of an arahant?
One should not say so... pe ...
Is there a killer of an arahant?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is there such a thing as an untimely death for an Arahant?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is it not the case that there is no untimely death for an Arahant?
Yes, [it is].

Then, when one deprives an Arahant of life, does he deprive him of life while life still exists and a remainder of life remains, or does he deprive him of life when life no longer exists and no remainder of life remains?
"If one deprives of life while life still exists and a remainder of life remains.
If indeed one deprives of life while life still exists and a remainder of life remains, then indeed, it should not be said:
"There is no untimely death for an Arahant."
If one deprives of life when there is no life remaining, but only a remnant of life, is there no such thing as a murderer of an Arahant?
One should not say so… [as before]… Is there no untimely death for an Arahant?
“Yes,” [you reply].
“Then would poison not take effect in the body of an Arahant, nor would a weapon take effect, nor would fire take effect?
You should not say so …pe…
But would not poison affect the body of an Arahant, would a weapon affect it, and would fire affect it? Yes.
If indeed poison would affect the body of an Arahant, a weapon would affect it, and fire would affect it, then surely you ought not say: [that he is invulnerable].
“There is no untimely death for an arahant.
Would poison not take effect in the body of an arahant? Would a weapon not take effect? Would fire not take effect? Yes.
Is there no such thing as a murderer of an arahant?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Is there untimely death for an arahant?
“Yes, [they do].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, I do not say that there is the exhaustion of intentional kamma that has been performed and accumulated without its being experienced’?”
"And that, moreover, either in this very life, upon rebirth, or at some other subsequent time.
Is there such a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, there is no untimely death for an Arahant.
The discussion on the absence of untimely death for an Arahant is concluded.
